cells.tense: Here, with your hand in the middle of the true thing, the fair call comes without arithmetic.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Take one small murky call and settle it by the sense of right already in you, before you weigh options or explain the choice to anyone.
cells.core:
You can step into a fog without needing the far side lit, and you can tell what's fair while you do it. Where what grew from patient change gets gathered, the count usually comes to you whole. You make this call and that call and they hold, and nobody sees the compass that made them, only the clear result. In the middle of not knowing what's next, the right first move still shows up.
There is a move you keep circling. It has a small unfairness in it, and you have been treating the fog as the reason not to look. The quietly known free thing still works there. Judge that one case, privately, and then do what the judgment says. You may still not see the road beyond it. Fairness does not need the road; it needs the step.
cells.sheetLine: A compass still works in fog.
cells.verb: gathering what patient change grew, here where the road ahead won't be visible past one more step
cells.place: moving through fog on just enough light for the next step

cells.tense: Ahead of all of it, the harvest is being audited before it has even ripened.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Give something you love a long unhurried stretch — an evening, one song — with no task attached, staying past the urge to figure out where it goes.
cells.core:
You are out past the edge of what is known — tallying streams that have not finished, trying to name what is still ripening in your hands. It looks like foresight. Underneath, it is the fear that patience is a wager you have already lost, so the count is kept heavy and early. The next move can't be written yet, and you are writing it anyway.
Stop a moment beside the thing you care about. Sit with what the heart already knows. No explaining what it's for. Not a verdict on your caution — a minute off the demand that the future show itself. The feeling will settle back into its own depth, and the next step comes easier with your hands quieter.

cells.tense: The harvest door has closed behind you, and you are still standing in the doorway it could have been.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Choose the pace for the nearest task so thirty days of it stay possible, rather than one that burns clean by Thursday, and hold there.
cells.core:
The fog is still here, and you are back at a gate that already swung shut, going over whether you might have walked through it. What transformation grew is ready to be gathered, and you are not gathering it; you are still negotiating the terms of having waited at all. The next step doesn't need the road either.
Begin with the nearest honest thing at a pace you could keep for a month. No surge to catch up, no reckoning with the lost years first. This is how alignment returns — will and feeling moving the same direction, not the fast start that burns out by Thursday. The next stretch, held steady, is enough to begin.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where the structure is already yours.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Where you're handling this fog with someone, say the shape of it plainly — the count, the decision — before anyone has to ask you for it.
cells.core:
A structure is being carried, and the hands carrying it would say later they just fell in behind. What was gathered out of fog is real, and its shape lives in you already. You have been declining the word for it — the one saying you sorted it, weighed the ambiguities, handed people the route. They're standing where you put them, and the moving holds.
Put the frame on the table in the open. One room, one sentence about what this is and what happens from here. There is no argument to win and no credit to collect; there is a next step that only makes sense if the shape is said out loud. Do it before the questions start. Let the fact that it was yours be seen out loud — by you, first.
